title: Formula and Fact Sheet
sub: Every formula and must-know fact in one place. There is no formula sheet on the real test, so learn these by heart.
label: Quick Reference
html:
Arithmetic and Percents

Topic Rule or formula
Order of operations Parentheses → Exponents → Multiply/Divide (left to right) → Add/Subtract (left to right)
Percent equation Part = Percent × Whole
Percent change (New − Original) ÷ Original × 100%
Sale price Price × (1 − discount rate)
Price with tax Price × (1 + tax rate)
Original price from sale price Sale price ÷ (1 − discount rate)
Simple interest I = P × r × t (t in years)
Average (mean) Sum ÷ number of values
Missing value for a target average Target average × count − sum of known values
Distance D = R × T
Average speed Total distance ÷ total time
Work together (two workers) Time = (A × B) ÷ (A + B)
Probability Favorable outcomes ÷ total outcomes
Independent events (A and B) P(A) × P(B)

Algebra

Topic Rule or formula
Exponents am · an = am+n; am ÷ an = am−n; (am)n = amn; a0 = 1; a−n = 1an
Special products (a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2; (a − b)2 = a2 − 2ab + b2; (a + b)(a − b) = a2 − b2
Quadratic formula x = −b ± √(b2 − 4ac)2a
Inequalities Flip the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number
Slope m = (y2 − y1)(x2 − x1)
Line y = mx + b (m = slope, b = y-intercept)
Parallel / perpendicular Same slope / negative reciprocal slopes
Distance between points √((x2 − x1)2 + (y2 − y1)2)
Midpoint ((x1 + x2)2, (y1 + y2)2)

  • Pythagorean theorem: a2 + b2 = c2. Triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25.
  • 45-45-90: x, x, x√2. 30-60-90: x, x√3, 2x.
  • Complementary angles total 90°; supplementary angles total 180°; vertical angles are equal.

Electronics

Topic Rule or formula
Ohm's law E = I × R; I = E ÷ R; R = E ÷ I
Power P = E × I = I2 × R = E2 ÷ R
Series resistance RT = R1 + R2 + ... (current same everywhere; voltages add up)
Parallel resistance RT = (R1 × R2) ÷ (R1 + R2); equal resistors: R ÷ n (voltage same on each branch)
Transformer V2 ÷ V1 = N2 ÷ N1 (more secondary turns = step up)
Batteries In series, voltages add; in parallel, voltage stays the same
Resistor colors Black 0, Brown 1, Red 2, Orange 3, Yellow 4, Green 5, Blue 6, Violet 7, Gray 8, White 9; Gold ±5%, Silver ±10%
Units Volt (V), amp (A), ohm (Ω), watt (W), farad (F), henry (H), hertz (Hz)
U.S. household power 120 V AC at 60 Hz
Wire gauge Smaller number = thicker wire = more current capacity

Mechanical

Topic Rule or formula
Work W = F × d
Power P = W ÷ t; 1 hp = 550 ft-lb/s ≈ 746 W
Mechanical advantage MA = load ÷ effort = effort distance ÷ load distance
Lever Effort × effort arm = Load × load arm
Lever classes Fulcrum in middle = 1st; Load in middle = 2nd; Effort in middle = 3rd
Pulleys MA = number of rope sections supporting the moving load
Wheel and axle MA = wheel radius ÷ axle radius
Inclined plane MA = length ÷ height
Screw Each turn advances one pitch; MA = 2π × handle length ÷ pitch
Gears TeethA × rpmA = TeethB × rpmB; meshing gears reverse direction
Belts DiameterA × rpmA = DiameterB × rpmB; crossed belt reverses direction
Springs F = kx; series springs stretch more, parallel springs stretch less
Pressure P = F ÷ A; hydraulics: F1 ÷ A1 = F2 ÷ A2
Fluids Pressure grows with depth; narrow pipe = faster flow and lower pressure
Beam on two supports Each support's share = load × (distance from load to the other support) ÷ span
